results.topic: ECC orchestration machinery deep-dive (Workflow pilot, gates, GAN loop, Santa, verification/checkpoints, PRP/PRD, loops, hooks, packaging): what HackForge should steal, adapt or skip
key_findings: ECC's single native Workflow, workflows/orch-review.workflow.js (about 300 lines), is its best orchestration code and fails closed at every layer: bad args throw; a dead reviewer forces CHANGES_REQUESTED; findings are deduped on the evidence snippet before verification (README: 11 raw collapsed to 4 unique); the schema itself requires a `proof` on HIGH/CRITICAL findings; a blocker is cleared only when the verifier refutes it with isReal=false and confidence >= 0.8. Unverifiable or uncertain blockers stay blocking.

The pilot is half-wired. commands/orch-review.md passes a relative scriptPath (workflows/orch-review.workflow.js) that only resolves inside the ECC repo, and installer wiring is listed as a follow-up. Its README says the verifier defaults to 'refuted' when uncertain, but the code keeps uncertain findings blocking. A null thunk result would be silently dropped by `.filter(Boolean)` (theoretical fail-open). There are no tests. Current Claude Code auto-discovers plugin workflows/*.js as /<plugin>:<meta.name>, so it should be invoked by name.

ECC's gates are prose only. The orch-pipeline Gate 1 (after plan) and Gate 2 (before every commit) are instructions to the model; no hook or state file enforces them. Every orchestrated loop except the pilot runs through the Task tool in the main context (gan-build, santa-loop) or through `claude -p` bash scripts (scripts/gan-harness.sh).

Patterns worth taking from orch-pipeline: a size classifier where ceremony scales with blast radius (state the tier in one line so the user can override it), planning docs as the only handoff with no hidden state, and an MVP built as thin vertical slices with one end-to-end path first.

The GAN loop (skills/gan-style-harness, commands/gan-build.md, agents/gan-*.md) has the right core: a separate, ruthlessly strict evaluator testing the live app via Playwright; feedback passed as files; the evaluator never fixes; plateau stop; honest reporting of the eval mode actually achieved; an anti-AI-slop list. Its defaults are wrong for a hackathon: 15 iterations, threshold 7.0, a 12-16 feature spec. Published cost is about $125-200 and 4-6 hours per run. The sprint contract from the Anthropic paper is never implemented, the dev-server lifecycle is left to the generator, and the score is scraped from markdown with awk.

Anthropic's harness-design post (2026-03-24) dropped sprint decomposition for frontier models and moved to a single end-of-build evaluator pass. Its guiding rule is to start with the simplest solution and add complexity only when needed. HackForge should cap evaluation at about 3 rounds per milestone plus one final pass.

Santa method: two context-isolated reviewers with the same rubric, both must PASS, fresh reviewers each round, maximum 3 rounds, then escalate to a human. santa-loop adds an optional Codex/Gemini reviewer for model diversity. It suits non-deterministic checks: pitch, README and Devpost claims, fake stats and links, and a final pre-submission go/no-go. It does not belong on every code change.

loop-design-check is the most transferable doc: machine-decidable goals, a done-criterion plus a boundary (anti-Goodhart), an independent deterministic judge, Build may not edit acceptance conditions, a retry cap, and 5 failure modes (worst: gating only on 'tests pass', so the agent deletes tests). autonomous-loops adds the de-sloppify cleanup pass, a SHARED_TASK_NOTES file to bridge fresh contexts, and uniqueness by assigning each parallel agent its own creative direction.

The hooks worth stealing: config-protection.js blocks edits that weaken existing lint/format configs (an anti-Goodhart hook); block-no-verify stops agents bypassing git hooks; stop-format-typecheck batches format and tsc once per response under a time budget; blocking hooks fail closed on truncated stdin; ECC_HOOK_PROFILE (minimal/standard/strict) and ECC_DISABLED_HOOKS give runtime control, with plugin userConfig toggles.

Bloat, quantified: 71 agents, 311 skills, 97 commands; about 123K characters (~30K tokens) of skill/agent/command descriptions; 27 hook entries across 8 events. GateGuard (2,574 lines) denies the first edit of every file. A dev-server hook forces tmux. A roughly 1.3 KB inline `node -e` root resolver is repeated in every hook. There are at least 8 overlapping planning entry points and 5+ review surfaces, and TDD with 80% coverage is mandatory. All of this is wrong for 24-48 hours.

Packaging: plugin slug `ecc` (install id ecc@ecc) is kept short because MCP tool names over 64 characters broke strict gateways. `mcpServers: {}` opts out of auto-loading the root .mcp.json. userConfig exposes hooks_enabled and hook_profile. The marketplace entry uses source './' and strict:false. There is a separate npx ecc-universal installer with profiles and modules across 15 harnesses; workflows/ appears in no install module.

ECC's PLUGIN_SCHEMA_NOTES.md is partly stale against the current official manifest reference. `agents` is a valid field, but as a list of .md file paths, not directories. `hooks` now merges with hooks/hooks.json. `name` is the only required field; `version` pins users to that version. workflows/ and bin/ are auto-discovered. claude plugin validate --strict and plugin evals exist.

Workflows cannot accept mid-run user input, so human gates must sit between workflows. Platform limits: 16 concurrent agents, 1,000 agents per run, 4,096 items per parallel/pipeline call, a 'Large workflow' warning above 25 agents or 1.5M tokens, size guideline medium (small on Pro). A bundled /deep-research workflow already exists and can serve HackForge's research phase.

recommendations.name: Port orch-review as hf-review workflow
recommendations.what: Copy the fail-closed skeleton: validate args and throw on bad input; one parallel reviewer per dimension with a schema; dedup barrier keyed on file plus normalized evidence; adversarially verify only CRITICAL/HIGH; return bounded error labels.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: This is the only proven native-Workflow pattern in ECC and it gives trustworthy pre-ship review without filling the main context. Add three fixes: count null thunks so a blocker can never vanish; keep uncertain security findings blocking but downgrade uncertain quality findings to advisory; name it so it doesn't collide with a skill or command.
recommendations.how: Model it on ECC workflows/orch-review.workflow.js (MIT, read-only reference). Save as hackforge/workflows/hf-review.js, invoked as /hf:review. Do not use a relative scriptPath.
recommendations.cost_auth: No auth. About 2-6 agents per run.

recommendations.name: Three hackathon gates at workflow boundaries + auto-checkpoints
recommendations.what: Gate A (idea lock), Gate B (scope lock: MVP slices plus demo script), Gate C (ship/submit). Between gates, take automatic checkpoints (git tag hf-cp-N, preview URL, smoke status) instead of ECC's per-commit Gate 2.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Workflows can't take mid-run input, and ECC's gates are prose only. Keeping gates few and at workflow boundaries preserves speed while keeping humans in charge of the decisions that matter.
recommendations.how: Store gate state in .hackforge/state.json. An optional PreToolUse hook (hf:scope-lock) denies src/ edits until scope_locked is true, in the 'safe' profile only. Adapted from skills/orch-pipeline/SKILL.md (two gates + size classifier) and commands/checkpoint.md.
recommendations.cost_auth: None.

recommendations.name: Demo-eval loop (adapted GAN generator/evaluator)
recommendations.what: Workflow /hf:demo-eval runs three judges in parallel: a golden-path Playwright runner, a design critic using the anti-slop list, and a skeptical-judge persona. All score against rubric.json, which is built from the hackathon's actual judging criteria. The generator fixes in the main loop between rounds. A slice contract is written before code. At most 3 rounds per milestone, a plateau stop after 1 round without improvement, and one final end pass.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: This keeps ECC's best insight (a separate strict evaluator, feedback via files, honest reporting of the eval mode achieved) without its 15-iteration, $125-200, 4-6 hour default. It also adds the sprint contract that ECC never implemented.
recommendations.how: Base it on agents/gan-evaluator.md (strictness, calibration, edge-case battery), agents/gan-generator.md (anti-slop list) and commands/gan-build.md (plateau rule). Use Workflow schemas instead of awk score parsing. Provide an idempotent `hf dev up` script that the evaluator calls first.
recommendations.cost_auth: Playwright MCP or Claude browser tools needed. Tokens scale with rounds; use the budget global.

recommendations.name: Judge-file protection hook (generalized config-protection)
recommendations.what: PreToolUse on Write/Edit/MultiEdit exits 2 when an existing rubric.json, slices/*/contract.md, tests/smoke/** or lint/format config is edited outside the scoping phase.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: It enforces loop-design-check's 'Build may not edit acceptance conditions' rule mechanically. This prevents the classic Goodhart failure where the agent weakens tests or the rubric to pass.
recommendations.how: Adapt ECC scripts/hooks/config-protection.js. Write it as "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}"/scripts/hooks/protect-judge.js in hackforge/hooks/hooks.json, not with the inline node -e bootstrap.
recommendations.cost_auth: None.

recommendations.name: Git/secret guard before push/deploy
recommendations.what: PreToolUse on Bash: block --no-verify, -c core.hooksPath=, force-push to main, and `git add .env*`. Before git push or deploy, run gitleaks if installed, otherwise a regex scan for sk-, AKIA, ghp_ and private-key headers.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Hackathon repos are usually made public for judging. ECC's commit-time secret check runs only in its strict profile, but leaked keys are a real and common hackathon failure.
recommendations.how: Adapt scripts/hooks/block-no-verify.js and the secret detection in scripts/hooks/pre-bash-commit-quality.js. Fail closed when stdin is truncated, as pre-bash-dispatcher.js does.
recommendations.cost_auth: Optional gitleaks binary. Ask before installing anything.

recommendations.name: Lean one-pager PRD (from plan-prd)
recommendations.what: Problem, user, hypothesis ('We believe X will solve Y for Z; we'll know when M'), MVP, explicit out-of-scope, demo script, judging-criteria map, and a milestone status table. Apply the anti-fluff rule: write 'TBD - needs validation via {method}' instead of inventing requirements.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: It replaces ECC's 8 overlapping planning flows with one fast artifact that feeds the slice plan and the rubric.
recommendations.how: Adapt commands/plan-prd.md, plus the 'NOT Building' list and per-task VALIDATE fields from commands/prp-plan.md and the Sizing & Phasing section of agents/planner.md. Ship as skill hackforge/skills/onepager/SKILL.md.
recommendations.cost_auth: None.

recommendations.name: Santa dual review for pitch and submission
recommendations.what: Two context-isolated reviewers (fact-checker and judge persona) use the same objective rubric. Both must pass. Fresh reviewers each round, at most 2 rounds, then escalate to the humans. Applies to the deck, demo script, README and Devpost text, and to the final pre-submission checklist.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Hallucinated stats, links and sponsor-API claims in a pitch are not caught by deterministic checks. Santa is ECC's strongest semantic-verification pattern.
recommendations.how: Adapt skills/santa-method/SKILL.md (verdict gate, rubric table, fresh reviewers) as workflow hackforge/workflows/hf-pitch.js. Codex or Gemini as reviewer B is optional and only used if already installed (see commands/santa-loop.md).
recommendations.cost_auth: About 2-3x generation tokens per round. Codex/Gemini CLIs need their own auth; don't require them.

recommendations.name: Idea fan-out with assigned directions + council
recommendations.what: N idea agents, each assigned a distinct angle (sponsor-API-first, pain-first, wow-demo-first, data-first...), scored by a judge panel against rubric.json plus feasibility in the remaining hours. Then a Skeptic/Pragmatist/Critic council reviews the top 3, each seeing only the question and compact context, and the main agent writes its own position first.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Assigning directions guarantees diversity instead of hoping for it (Infinite Agentic Loop). The council's anti-anchoring setup produces a defensible Gate A decision.
recommendations.how: Patterns from skills/autonomous-loops/SKILL.md section 3 and skills/council/SKILL.md. Implement as hackforge/workflows/hf-ideate.js using pipeline() and schemas.
recommendations.cost_auth: Fewer than 10 agents by default; scale down on Pro (size guideline small).

recommendations.name: Demo-readiness loop + checkpoints
recommendations.what: /hf:ready runs: clean install, build and typecheck, golden-path smoke against local and deployed URLs, secret scan, README/.env.example check, then a READY/NOT READY report. Checkpoints record git tag, preview URL and smoke status, with a one-step rollback to the last green checkpoint.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: This replaces ECC's coverage-heavy verification-loop with the checks judges actually experience.
recommendations.how: Adapt skills/verification-loop/SKILL.md (report format; pipefail plus `sed -n` instead of head) and commands/checkpoint.md (checkpoint log).
recommendations.cost_auth: Deploy provider CLI auth belongs to the user. Never enter credentials.

recommendations.name: Minimal hook set with profiles
recommendations.what: Five hooks: protect-judge, git-guard, scope-lock (safe only), a Stop batch typecheck with a 60s budget, and SessionStart/PreCompact injection and snapshot of .hackforge/STATE.md (at most 1,500 chars). Profiles off/fast/safe via plugin userConfig plus an HF_DISABLED_HOOKS env var.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: This keeps ECC's enforcement value without its 27 entries and per-call process-spawn latency.
recommendations.how: Model on hooks/README.md runtime controls, scripts/hooks/run-with-flags.js and scripts/hooks/stop-format-typecheck.js + post-edit-accumulator.js. Use "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}" or exec-form args.
recommendations.cost_auth: None.

recommendations.name: Plugin packaging: slug `hf`, skills-first
recommendations.what: .claude-plugin/plugin.json with name 'hf', version and userConfig hook_profile. Layout: skills/ (12 or fewer, no commands/), agents/ (8 or fewer, listed as .md files if declared), workflows/*.js (auto-discovered as /hf:<name>), hooks/hooks.json. Omit mcpServers unless HackForge actually ships servers. Install with /plugin marketplace add <owner>/hackforge, then /plugin install hf@hackforge.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: A short slug keeps MCP tool names under 64 characters and commands short. Skills-first matches the current plugin docs. Auto-discovered workflows avoid ECC's relative-path bug.
recommendations.how: Validate with `claude plugin validate ./hackforge --strict`. Optionally add evals/ and run `claude plugin eval`. Do not copy ECC's PLUGIN_SCHEMA_NOTES rules ('no agents field', 'version mandatory'); they are stale.
recommendations.cost_auth: None. Requires a public GitHub repo for marketplace install.

recommendations.name: Steal small agents: build fixer and judge
recommendations.what: hf-fixer uses a minimal-diff contract (no refactor or architecture changes; success = build green with under 5% of each affected file changed). hf-judge uses the gan-evaluator strictness prompt and calibration table.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: A 3 a.m. build break needs a narrow fixer, not a redesign, and the judge's strictness is what makes the eval loop useful.
recommendations.how: Adapt agents/build-error-resolver.md and agents/gan-evaluator.md. Keep the 'Prompt Defense Baseline' only on agents that read untrusted web content.
recommendations.cost_auth: None.

recommendations.name: Skip ECC's heavy machinery
recommendations.what: Do not import: multi-* commands (external ccg-workflow runtime), GateGuard, the tmux dev-server blocker, continuous-learning/governance/cost hooks, the inline node -e bootstrap, the operator-approval ledger, Ralphinho merge queue, continuous PR loop, NanoClaw, dmux, epic-*, plan-orchestrate, prp-prd, the architect agent, 20 language reviewers, the mandatory TDD/80% coverage rule, installer manifests, agent.yaml.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Each adds setup, latency or ceremony that costs hours with no effect on demo quality.
recommendations.how: Reference paths are listed in the report's Steal/Adapt/Skip table, rows 34-44.
recommendations.cost_auth: n/a

open_questions: If a plugin ships workflows/x.js (meta.name 'x') and also skills/x or commands/x.md, which one does /hf:x resolve to? ECC's orch-review may already collide. Test with --plugin-dir and claude plugin validate.
Does a dev server started with Bash run_in_background by one workflow subagent survive for later evaluator agents, or must the main session or the evaluator own the server lifecycle?
Are Playwright MCP or Claude browser tools reliably reachable from workflow agents through ToolSearch in all the surfaces HackForge targets (CLI, Desktop, cloud)?
Is reviewer prompt-cache sharing worth designing for (one agentType with the lens in the prompt, versus ECC's distinct agentTypes per reviewer)? Needs measurement.
On Pro plans the workflow size guideline defaults to 'small' (fewer than 5 agents). Should HackForge workflows scale down automatically via args or budget?
Do hackathon teams want the hard scope-lock hook, or only a prose gate plus a state flag? Validate in a dry run.
Claude Code's plugin and workflow features change quickly (several need v2.1.2xx or later). Recheck the manifest and workflow docs when HackForge is actually built.

results.topic: ECC research, product, demo and MCP surfaces: which parts to steal, adapt or skip for a hackathon flow (research -> idea -> build -> demo -> submit), what ECC lacks, and how it manages MCP context cost
key_findings: ECC has no hackathon layer. Across 311 skills there are 0 hits for 'hackathon', 'ideation', 'devpost' and 'user research'. 'brainstorm' appears once, in a manufacturing QA skill. Nothing covers idea generation, scoring against judging criteria, sponsor-prize mapping, demo scripts, pitch timing, submission checklists or deadline time-boxing. This is where HackForge has to build new.

Strong enough to steal nearly as-is: skills/ui-demo is a Playwright demo recorder with Discover->Rehearse->Record phases, a rehearsal selector gate, cursor and subtitle overlays, and fixed pacing numbers. skills/frontend-slides is a single-file HTML deck with a hard viewport-fit gate, density limits, 12 style presets and a Playwright PDF export script. skills/search-first adds a tool preflight and an adopt/extend/compose/build matrix. skills/council (4 voices, anti-anchoring) re-casts well as a judge panel.

Good ideas inside generic skills, worth adapting: deep-research (sub-questions, 15-30 sources, 3-5 deep reads, untrusted-source rules); research-ops (labels each claim as sourced fact, user-provided, inference or recommendation); product-lens (7-question diagnostic plus ICE scoring); plan-prd (anti-fluff 'TBD - needs validation via {method}' rule and a hypothesis template); orch-build-mvp ('thin vertical slices, one end-to-end path first'); investor-materials ('all materials agree' from one source of truth); marketing-campaign (copy hard-bans and the 5-second test).

gan-style-harness gets the core idea right: a separate strict evaluator that drives the live app (confirmed by Anthropic's 2026-03-24 harness article). It costs 4-6 h and $125-200, though. HackForge should keep the evaluator but score against the event's judging rubric and cap it at 2-3 passes by wall clock. agents/gan-evaluator.md also depends on mcp__playwright__* tools, which ECC no longer enables by default.

Weak or generic for hackathons, skip: deployment-patterns (blue-green, canary, k8s), product-capability (SRS contracts), github-ops (maintainer triage), data-scraper-agent (a scraper product template with stale Gemini 2.0 model names), exa-search (a vendor wrapper), contexts/*.md (20-line mode prompts), and rules/common/* (mandatory TDD, 80% coverage, a reviewer after every change). The rules are anti-demo-first and should be overridden.

MCP defaults: the ECC Claude plugin ships zero MCPs ('mcpServers': {} in .claude-plugin/plugin.json). This deliberately opts out of root .mcp.json auto-discovery and avoids tool names over 64 characters. The root .mcp.json has a single pinned default, chrome-devtools-mcp@1.10.1. Everything else is an opt-in entry in a 34-entry catalog at mcp-configs/mcp-servers.json.

docs/MCP-CONNECTOR-POLICY.md gives a two-prong rule for any default connector: it must be universal, AND MCP must beat a CLI/API wrapped in a skill (session state, streaming, auth handshake, structured browsing). A June 2026 audit applied it and dropped github, context7, exa, memory, playwright and sequential-thinking for CLIs, REST calls or native features. HackForge should adopt this rule outright.

ECC's context-cost guidance is partly stale. 'Keep <10 MCPs / <80 tools; 200k can become 70k' predates Claude Code's default tool search, where only tool names and server instructions load and schemas are deferred. Costs that remain: per-call output size (Playwright snapshots run about 10-30k tokens), alwaysLoad servers, auth and connect latency, and supply-chain drift. ECC's own longform guide concedes lazy loading 'mostly solved' the context issue.

ECC contradicts itself in several places. deep-research requires firecrawl or exa MCP, but neither is a default. documentation-lookup still says 'via Context7 MCP'. token-optimization.md claims memory MCP is on by default. The catalog fails ECC's own mcp-dependency-review: 17 of its 18 npx/uvx entries are mutable (3 @latest, 14 bare names). Only mcp-atlassian==0.21.0 is pinned.

Harmful pattern to avoid: the longform guide loads contexts/*.md with `claude --system-prompt "$(cat ...)"`. Per the Claude Code CLI reference, --system-prompt replaces the entire default prompt, dropping tool guidance and safety instructions. Use --append-system-prompt-file, output styles, or phase skills instead.

Hackathon judges typically weight innovation, technical work and impact at 20-25% each, demo/presentation at 15-20% and completeness at 10-15%. Some events add a pass/fail check that required APIs were used. Judges reward working live demos, real data and a specific target user. They penalize mockups, hardcoded data, demo crashes and thin wrappers. ECC's ICE scoring captures none of these. HackForge needs a rubric weighted by the event's own criteria, with feasibility and demo-ability gates and sponsor-prize expected value.

recommendations.name: hf-demo (port of ECC ui-demo)
recommendations.what: Playwright demo-video recorder: Discover -> Rehearse (ensureVisible gate) -> Record, with cursor and subtitle overlays and the pacing numbers. Adds a timed narrative script, seed/reset scripts for repeatable demo state, ffmpeg conversion to MP4 with loudness normalization and captions, and a pre-loaded live-demo fallback video.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: A working, polished demo is the top judging factor and a demo crash is the top penalty. ECC's skill is the best demo asset in the repo but has no narrative, state reset or fallback.
recommendations.how: Copy the helper functions and checklist from skills/ui-demo/SKILL.md into skills/hf-demo/ and templates/demo/record.cjs. Run `node demo/record.cjs --rehearse`, then `node demo/record.cjs`, then `ffmpeg -i demo.webm -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -af loudnorm demo.mp4`.
recommendations.cost_auth: Free; needs Playwright and ffmpeg installed locally. No MCP.

recommendations.name: hf-pitch (port of frontend-slides + investor-materials Golden Rule)
recommendations.what: Single-file HTML deck with the viewport-fit gate, density limits and style presets, reordered into a hackathon flow: hook, problem, solution, live demo, how it works, sponsor tech, impact, next + team. Adds per-slide timing (about 450 words for 3 min), speaker notes and PDF export.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Demo/presentation is 15-20% of the score and frames every other criterion. ECC's slide engine is strong, but its deck flow is built for investors (raise, use of funds).
recommendations.how: Copy skills/frontend-slides/{SKILL.md,STYLE_PRESETS.md,viewport-base.css,html-template.md,scripts/export-pdf.sh} into skills/hf-pitch/. Replace the deck flow with report section 6.6.
recommendations.cost_auth: Free; Playwright for PDF export.

recommendations.name: hf-ideate with judging-weighted rubric + council-as-judges
recommendations.what: Generates 15 ideas from theme x sponsor APIs x pain evidence x team skills, then scores them. Scores use HACKATHON.md criteria weights, a feasibility gate, a 1.5x demo-ability multiplier, sponsor-prize expected value as tiebreak, and a novelty gate. A panel of fresh subagents in judge personas (technical, impact, sponsor, skeptic) then critiques the shortlist, with the orchestrator committing to a pick first.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: ECC has no ideation at all, and product-lens ICE scoring ignores the event's own judging criteria. This is HackForge's main differentiator.
recommendations.how: New skill. Reuse the product-lens Mode 1 questions and the council workflow and prompt shape (skills/product-lens/SKILL.md, skills/council/SKILL.md). Rubric is in report section 6.1.
recommendations.cost_auth: Model tokens only; 3-4 short subagents.

recommendations.name: /hf-kickoff -> HACKATHON.md single source of truth
recommendations.what: Captures from the rules page: theme, eligibility, deadline and timezone, judging criteria with weights, sponsor prizes with requirements, submission fields, video limits, and team roles. Every later artifact (deck, Devpost copy, README, narration) reads from it.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Every downstream decision is scored against this. It prevents ineligible or off-rubric builds and applies investor-materials' 'all materials agree' principle.
recommendations.how: New command; template in templates/HACKATHON.md. Kick off scaffolding and research in parallel, following the longform guide's two-instance pattern.
recommendations.cost_auth: Free; one WebFetch or bdata scrape of the rules page.

recommendations.name: hf-research (adapted deep-research + research-ops + search-first preflight)
recommendations.what: Tool-agnostic research. Provider ladder: WebSearch/WebFetch -> bdata -> optional Parallel/Exa/Firecrawl. Runs a preflight that reports skipped channels. Budget: at most 25 searches, 6 deep reads, 3 parallel subagents. Every claim gets an evidence label and date. Output is RESEARCH.md with pain evidence, sponsor API capabilities and limits, datasets, and prior art (Devpost galleries, past winners).
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: ECC's deep-research is hard-wired to MCPs it no longer enables, has no time box, and produces essay-style reports rather than decisions.
recommendations.how: Keep the 'Untrusted Sources' block from skills/deep-research/SKILL.md verbatim. Take the output labels from skills/research-ops/SKILL.md and the Step 0 preflight from skills/search-first/SKILL.md.
recommendations.cost_auth: Free with built-in tools; bdata is paid per request (cheap). Exa, Firecrawl or Parallel need keys (Parallel claims anonymous use works; unverified).

recommendations.name: hf-spec (demo-first PRD)
recommendations.what: Lean PRD where the golden-path demo script is the spec. Must-haves are whatever appears on screen. Includes a won't-build list, a fake-vs-real ledger, and thin vertical slices with slice 1 as the end-to-end golden path.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Judges penalize mockups and hardcoded data, and they ask about what is real at Q&A. Slicing keeps a demoable build at every point.
recommendations.how: Adapt commands/plan-prd.md (hypothesis template, `TBD - needs validation via {method}`) and the slicing line from skills/orch-build-mvp/SKILL.md.

results.topic: Best MCP servers and CLIs for research and ideation inside Claude Code (late 2026), with a tiered zero-key / with-keys / optional stack for HackForge
key_findings: Claude Code now defers all MCP tool definitions by default (tool search). Only tool names and server instructions, capped at 4,096 chars per server, load at session start (code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp). The real context costs are now overlapping tools that confuse tool choice and large result payloads (MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS defaults to 25k, with a warning above 10k). Schema size matters much less than it did in 2025.

A live probe on 2026-10-15 measured definition sizes and per-call results for keyless servers. Parallel: 2 tools, about 3.6k tokens of definitions, about 5.1k tokens per search, 1.3 s. Firecrawl keyless: 3 tools, about 6.9k tokens of definitions. DeepWiki: 3 tools, about 0.4k tokens. Grep: 1 tool, about 0.8k tokens. Context7: 2 tools, about 1.3k tokens. HF anonymous: 4 tools, about 5.1k tokens. Community HN server: about 7.9k tokens. Exa keyless was rate-limited on the first call, and the raw arXiv API returned 429.

A 2026 study (arXiv 2607.10198) ran Brave, Tavily and Firecrawl under one fixed agent. They scored 25, 25 and 26 out of 100 hard questions, but their union of correct answers was 44/100. HackForge should pair two complementary providers rather than load five similar search MCPs.

ECC's June 2026 audit (docs/MCP-CONNECTOR-POLICY.md) ships one default MCP and moves GitHub, Context7, Exa and Playwright into CLI-backed skills. It drops memory and sequential-thinking entirely. HackForge should adopt the same rule: an MCP only where it is universal and genuinely beats a skill-wrapped CLI.

A strong zero-key core exists and worked live today: built-in WebSearch/WebFetch, Parallel Search MCP, DeepWiki MCP, Grep by Vercel MCP, Context7 (keyless at low limits), Hugging Face MCP (anonymous or OAuth), and alphaXiv (free OAuth account). HN Algolia, OpenAlex and GitHub REST are better as curl skills than as MCPs.

Bright Data MCP changed this week. v3.0.0 (2026-10-11) removed 46 web_data_* tools in favor of search_scrapers, get_scraper_details and run_scraper over 1,200+ scrapers. v3.1.0 (2026-10-15) removed PRO_MODE and turned all 32 tools on by default, so guides mentioning 'pro mode', '&pro=1' or web_data_* are stale. The free tier is 5,000 requests a month with no card, then $1.50 per 1k. The hosted server also advertises OAuth with bearer-in-header, so the documented ?token= URL param is not needed.

The Bright Data CLI (bdata, already installed) is the most practical social-signal source. Its catalog has Reddit Posts (gd_lvz8ah06191smkebj4, discover_by_keyword or subreddit), Reddit Comments, YouTube Videos (gd_lk56epmy2i5g7lzu0k, discover_by_keyword with dates), X Posts (by URL or profile only) and GitHub repository. It has no Google Trends or Product Hunt scraper.

Reddit blocked logged-out JSON and ended self-service API keys in November 2025, so keyless Reddit MCPs such as reddit-mcp-buddy only browse via RSS with null scores. X API is pay-per-use (secondary: about $5 per 1k posts). Google Trends has no usable free API: the official API is a gated alpha and pytrends was archived in April 2025. HN is effortless via the free Algolia API.

Pricing in 2026 (some figures secondary): Brave dropped its free tier for $5 of monthly credit with a card required. Tavily gives 1,000 free credits a month and was acquired by Nebius in February 2026. Exa costs $7 per 1k search-with-contents. Perplexity has no free tier ($5 per 1k for the Search API). Parallel's paid API is about $1–5 per 1k with $5 of monthly credit, and its MCP is keyless. Firecrawl gives 1,000 free credits a month, including a keyless hosted endpoint limited to scrape, search and parse.

GitHub's official remote MCP (api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/) supports per-URL toolsets (/x/repos/readonly) and the headers X-MCP-Toolsets, X-MCP-Readonly, X-MCP-Tools and X-MCP-Lockdown. The official Claude Code command is claude mcp add-json with a Bearer PAT. For research, gh or REST in a skill is cheaper. ECC's catalog still lists the deprecated @modelcontextprotocol/server-github.

Doc and tool-name drift is common. DeepWiki's live tool is ask_wiki_question, while its docs say ask_question. Exa's hosted defaults are now web_search_exa and web_fetch_exa, but ECC's exa-search skill names get_code_context_exa and crawling_exa. Firecrawl's /v2/mcp-search endpoint, which carries the research and developer tools, requires OAuth.

OAuth-only servers (alphaXiv, HF ?login, Tavily OAuth) cannot authenticate under claude -p or the Agent SDK until someone signs in once interactively. HackForge Workflow scripts need a setup login step or keyless fallbacks.

Web content fetched by search agents is a demonstrated injection and poisoning vector (arXiv 2606.16821, 2609.06027). Bright Data's CONTENT_GATE and untrusted-content marking, plus GitHub's X-MCP-Lockdown, are worth enabling, and HackForge should corroborate pitch claims with at least 2 sources.

results.topic: Best MCP servers, CLIs, plugins, templates and services (late 2026) for building and shipping a hackathon MVP with Claude Code
key_findings: Anthropic's official marketplace claude-plugins-official (315 entries, checked today) has first-party plugins for vercel, supabase, stripe, figma, playwright, context7, chrome-devtools-mcp, cloudflare, convex, neon, firebase, expo, railway, render, netlify-skills, resend, sentry, huggingface-skills, frontend-design and others. Each bundles the vendor's MCP server, skills and slash commands. Install with `claude plugin install <name>@claude-plugins-official`. Where a plugin exists, HackForge should prefer it over hand-written MCP config.

Claude Code's MCP tool search is on by default: tool schemas load only when needed. So the cost of configuring a server is now small. The cost of large tool results (DOM trees, screenshots, logs) is still high. `.mcp.json` supports ${VAR} expansion; credential-like names such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY expand to empty in remote headers, so use your own variable names. A secret passed literally to `claude mcp add --header` is stored in plaintext in ~/.claude.json.

ECC's mcp-configs/mcp-servers.json is partly stale. @railway/mcp-server is deprecated (now `railway mcp install`). Magic MCP was renamed to 21st MCP (`npx @21st-dev/cli@latest init --client claude`) and old keys were reset. Cloudflare asks users to move from its per-product servers to one API MCP at https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp. fal, ElevenLabs and Supabase now have official hosted OAuth or key-header servers that replace the community or local ones. The local `uvx elevenlabs-mcp` is deprecated.

ECC's own MCP policy ships only one default server (chrome-devtools) and turns Context7, GitHub and Playwright into CLI-plus-skill workflows. Microsoft's Playwright MCP README also tells coding agents to prefer `@playwright/cli` with skills. A July 2026 test found the token gap between the two has largely closed, but the CLI is still the better default.

Supabase remote MCP: https://mcp.supabase.com/mcp?project_ref=...&read_only=true&features=..., authenticated by OAuth through /mcp with no access token needed. The free plan allows 2 active projects, and projects pause after 7 days of inactivity. So create or wake the project on the day, and always pin project_ref.

The Vercel MCP (https://mcp.vercel.com, OAuth) can now deploy code and query logs and analytics. The Vercel plugin (`npx plugins add vercel/vercel-plugin` or vercel@claude-plugins-official) adds /vercel:deploy, /vercel:env and skills. The Hobby plan is for non-commercial use. Give judges the production URL, because preview deployments may sit behind Vercel login (unverified default).

Stripe: `stripe agent setup` or `claude mcp add --transport http stripe https://mcp.stripe.com/` with OAuth. Gotcha: from December 2026 Stripe MCP rejects full-access secret keys and restricted keys without the Agent tag. Migrate to agent API keys by Nov 30, 2026. Refunds and payouts need a human to approve through a URL. Use only a sandbox during a hackathon.

Figma MCP (plugin figma@claude-plugins-official, or https://mcp.figma.com/mcp) allows only 6 tool calls per month on Starter, View or Collab seats. Real use needs a paid Dev or Full seat, so it only helps teams with a paid designer.

Context7: `npx ctx7 setup --claude` offers a CLI-plus-skills mode with no MCP (needs Node 22.13+). The remote MCP is https://mcp.context7.com/mcp with a free key. Vendor MCPs also carry their own docs-search tools (Supabase, Vercel, Stripe, Cloudflare, fal, Clerk, Expo).

Claude in Chrome (`claude --chrome`) needs a direct Pro, Max, Team or Enterprise plan and /login, and is disabled under API-key auth. It runs a visible browser only, records GIFs, and uses the user's real logins; a project's settings cannot turn it on. Claude Code Desktop also has a built-in Browser pane (.claude/launch.json + preview_start) and iOS Simulator control, observed in this environment.

From the bundled claude-api skill: default model claude-opus-5-5 at $4/$20 per million tokens; claude-sonnet-5-5 at $2/$10; claude-haiku-5-5 at $0.10/$0.50. Patterns from 2024-25 tutorials now return 400: disabling thinking or budget_tokens on Opus 5.5 (use effort instead), forced tool_choice, and assistant prefill. Thinking display defaults to omitted. Add server-side refusal fallbacks.

AI service facts: fal has an official hosted MCP at https://mcp.fal.ai/mcp (Bearer FAL_KEY, 9 tools including get_pricing). Replicate's is SSE at https://mcp.replicate.com/sse. The Hugging Face MCP is https://huggingface.co/mcp?login. Gradio's `launch(mcp_server=True)` turns a demo into an MCP server. Vercel AI Gateway gives $5 per month of free credit. OpenRouter free models allow 50 requests a day until $10 of lifetime purchases. Modal's Starter plan gives about $30 a month in credits (secondary sources).

Demo video tooling: Playwright video recording driven by a script (ECC's ui-demo skill, with a cursor overlay) doubles as a regression test. Remotion (`npx create-video@latest`, `npx skills add remotion-dev/skills`) is free for individuals and companies of up to 3 employees. HyperFrames by HeyGen (HTML to video, Apache-2.0) has a Claude Code plugin. For captions, use ElevenLabs Scribe v2 or Whisper, then burn them in with `ffmpeg -vf subtitles=x.srt`. results.topic: GitHub mining: repos HackForge should learn from or integrate (Claude Code harnesses, MCP lists and aggregators, hackathon tooling, pitch and demo tools, deep-research agents, idea validation, AI judging)
key_findings: I assessed 100+ repos (about 85 in the report's tables). The highest-signal hackathon repos are tiny and unknown: RikepilB/crafterwiki (4 stars), painbaba/hackathon-radar (0), Jazztinn/dontreadme (11), Esther2524/beautiful-hackathon-slides (36), SultanAlfaifi/rajih-engine (2). Each encodes one winning practice that no big harness has.

CrafterWIKI's /hack-plan (commands/hack-plan.md, ADR-004) fixes a demo-first phase order: Intake, Recon (rubric and lens weights, sponsor lanes, saturation), Patterns, 3 structurally different Angles, Judge-panel gate, Demo script and pitch, User gate, then Architecture, then an hourly build plan with code freeze and 2 rehearsals. Phase files are numbered and a run resumes from the first missing file. It also has a taxonomy of 23 winning 'mechanisms' and 15 'judging lenses'. Its own holdout test did not validate copying winners, so these are hypotheses.

hackathon-radar's thesis is that 'most hackathon losses are selection losses'. Its method maps saturation with Devpost search counts (e.g. 'agent' 35,559 projects, 'education' 26,603, 'kirana' 60), then deep-reads the 3 nearest competitors to confirm the gap. It also has a shot-by-shot 4-minute demo-video beat sheet (captions on, because judges watch muted).

ECC (71 agents / 97 commands / 311 skills) has deep-research, market-research, frontend-slides, ui-demo and remotion skills but no phase-ordered hackathon spine: no rubric intake, saturation analysis, judge panel or demo-first gate. That is HackForge's opening.

garrytan/gstack (136,577 stars) /office-hours has six forcing questions (demand reality, status quo, desperate specificity, narrowest wedge, observation, future-fit) and an explicit Builder Mode for hackathons. github/spec-kit's 'assess' extension (intake, research, define, shape, decide) ends in go / needs-clarification / kill. arslan70/haytham ends in GO/NO-GO/PIVOT and keeps a concept-anchor.json of invariants to stop idea drift.

Submission-package patterns all share one rule: never fabricate URLs, metrics or teammates. dontreadme maps the README to the rubric with a 'Judging Highlights' section and leaves TODO placeholders. beautiful-hackathon-slides makes a 9-phase HTML deck with a demo-video slot, 6 animated demo-slide fallbacks and a narration script timed to the video limit. get-convex/convex-hackathon-skill keeps a hackathon.md build log from git evidence.

Deep-research patterns to borrow: hyperresearch (3,865 stars) has a light tier (about 30-40 min) vs full (1.5-2.5h), a cite-check hard gate, an independence audit (syndicated copies count as one source) and resumable runs. dzhng/deep-research uses breadth and depth knobs in under 500 LoC. STORM uses perspective-guided questions. jina's loop runs until the token budget is spent. last30days-skill (64,441) ranks Reddit, HN, X and Polymarket signals by engagement.

Ideation and judging can be one deterministic Workflow script: isolated ideators (rajih-engine), evidence scout, parallel lens judges, bias auditor, chief judge with a confidence tier (ORCHESTRA), then an adversarial PRD attack (Quorum: Architect, Breaker, TDD Enforcer, Pragmatist, Judge).

AI first-pass judging is spreading. carmatthews/claude-code-hackathon says 'Claude will judge' and 'commit history is evidence'. BuildersClaw weights deployed-URL runtime judging at 30%. So HackForge should optimize for LLM judges and live-URL health, not only human judges.

State-on-disk patterns are mature: planning-with-files (3-file plan re-injected by a hook; its own measurement shows re-orientation dropping from 13.3 to 5.0 turns), StartupKit (YAML-frontmatter session state), GSD (fresh 200k-context executors in waves), ralph (prd.json passes:true as the stop condition), frankbria (dual-condition exit gate plus circuit breaker).

Distribution has converged on Claude Code plugin marketplaces plus Agent Skills (npx skills add, which supports 75+ agents). Plugin slugs are immutable in claude-plugins-official. hesreallyhim/ultracode-workflows claims plugins now ship native Workflow scripts as first-class components, but ray-amjad called the tool unreleased in May 2026. This needs verifying.

The ecosystem is huge and noisy: awesome-mcp-servers has about 4,259 entries, and a roundup reports about 24.4k repos with Claude Code plugin definitions by June 2026. Star counts are a weak signal, so tolkonepiu/best-of-mcp-servers (quality-ranked, weekly) and quemsah/awesome-claude-plugins (adoption metrics) are better selection data.

results.topic: Evidence-based hackathon winning playbook (AI/software hackathons 2025-2026, 24-48h and week-long virtual, teams of 1-4 using AI coding agents)
key_findings: Published rubrics differ a lot, so parse them before choosing an idea. MLH weights Technology, Design, Completion and Learning equally, and explicitly does NOT judge the pitch, the idea or code quality. Devpost sponsor events use Tech, Design, Impact and Idea at 25% each. Anthropic's Built with Opus 4.6 used Demo 30, Impact 25, Opus use 25, Depth 20 (from a copy of the rules in a winner's repo, not the official page). The Gemini 3 weights of Tech 40 / Innovation 30 / Impact 20 / Presentation 10 come only from third-party reprints.

There are hidden gates. OpenAI Build Week (Jul 2026) scored nothing until a pass/fail Stage 1 on theme fit and required API use. It broke ties on the first criterion listed, allowed judging by automated AI analysis, and did not require judges to run the app. The video and written submission must make the case on their own.

Judging formats: MLH expo gives about 4 minutes per judge visit (2 min demo, 1 min Q&A and scoring, 1 min travel), at least 3 judges per project, then a 3/2/1 stack ranking. ETHGlobal finalists get 4 min of demo plus 3 min of Q&A. Video limits are 2:00 (MLH digital), under 3:00 (Anthropic, OpenAI) and 2:00-4:00 (ETHGlobal).

2026 winners are mostly domain experts solving one narrow workflow with a quantified pain. Examples: CrossBeam (a lawyer; CA permits rejected 90%+ of the time, costing about $30k), TARA (road appraisal cut from weeks to 5 hours), Medkit (physician), veTriage (veterinarian), Pulse (cardiologist). Four of the five Opus 4.6 winners were not professional developers.

Patterns among winners: a deterministic core with AI at the interpretation layer; visible non-chat evidence (pitch curves, 3D, graphs, citations); a human approving consequential steps; multi-agent orchestration with verifiers (Tekton's isolated verifier subagents, Wrench Board's 5-6 parallel agents, Medkit's agentic grader); eval numbers shown on screen (Sim Francisco backtests); and visible iteration past v1 (Anthropic gives a 'Keep Thinking' prize for it).

Fatigue categories: generic 'AI chatbot for X', frontend-only chat wrappers, 'blockchain for Y', todo/notes apps, and dashboards that only display data. This is thinly sourced (one 2026 platform blog and one 2024 Reddit rant). The extended list (chat-with-PDF, travel planner, study buddy, resume reviewer) is my inference. Rescue recipe: narrow user + domain data + visible artifact + eval number + human approval.

Prize stacking rules vary by event. OpenAI Build Week allowed one prize per project. Docusign allowed several category prizes. ETHGlobal allows up to 3 partner prizes, each with a write-up that is the partner's only way to assess you. Sponsor tech has to be load-bearing and visible in the video; rubrics reward thorough or creative use, not logo-stuffing.

Timing guidance: Devpost and MLH say to leave 2-3 hours at the end for the video and submission. Masai says to submit at least 30 minutes early. An Anthropic winner said to reserve the final day of a week-long event for the video. My recommended 24h checkpoints: idea lock H2 (8%), skeleton deployed H7 (30%), core 'wow' working H13 (55%), feature freeze H18 (75%), video done H20.5 (85%), submitted H22 (92%).

Demo video structure (AngelHack 3-min split): 0:00-0:30 hook and problem, 0:30-2:00 demo (about half the runtime, with the 'aha' by 1:00), 2:00-2:30 the hard part plus model choice and how quality was measured, 2:30-3:00 impact and next steps. ETHGlobal rejects TTS/AI voiceover, sped-up footage, phone recordings and music-with-captions, and requires at least 720p. The live pitch needs at most 1 opening slide and 5 total.

Organizers now score AI-agent use rather than penalize it. Anthropic gives 25% to model use. OpenAI required a README describing the Codex collaboration plus a session ID, and counted it toward Tech and Idea. MLH and ETHGlobal require AI disclosure. ETHGlobal warns that fully AI-built projects without meaningful team contribution may be ineligible for partner prizes, and may disqualify projects whose history is one giant commit.

The prepared harness wins. The ECC author won the Anthropic x Forum Ventures hackathon with about 10 months of pre-built agents and skills, and his stated lesson was to load only the relevant skills to avoid context bloat. Opus 4.7 and 4.8 winners used spec-then-plan, parallel domain sessions, PRD plus about 50 tickets, eval-first, and an audit before each new feature.

Top failure modes: scope creep (teams typically reach about a quarter of their ambitions, per BuilderBase), a live demo with no fallback for flaky APIs, no deployment, auth walls (rules require free test access), exposed keys (GitGuardian: 23.8M secrets leaked on public GitHub in 2024, and 70% of those leaked in 2022 were still active), late or private or over-length videos, and teams unable to explain the AI-written differentiating logic in Q&A.

recommendations.name: /hf:rules rubric parser
recommendations.what: Command plus skill that scrapes the event and rules pages (Devpost, ETHGlobal, MLH, Cerebral Valley) into rubric.json. It captures criteria and weights, Stage-1 gates, video length and bans, the prize-stacking rule, team size, licence and pre-existing-code rules, and the deadline in local time.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Rubrics differ widely (MLH ignores the pitch; Anthropic gives the demo 30%), and Stage-1 gates and tie-break order decide outcomes. Every later step (scoring, judge simulation, submission validation) re-weights from this file.
recommendations.how: Use bdata scrape on the event's /rules and overview pages, then have an LLM extract into a fixed JSON schema. Fall back to the HackForge Default Rubric (D25/T20/I20/O15/S10/U10) when no rubric is published.
recommendations.cost_auth: bdata is paid per request but cheap; no auth needed for public rules pages

recommendations.name: idea-scorer subagent (HackForge Idea Score)
recommendations.what: Applies gates G1-G6 and then the formula IdeaScore = 20 x F x (0.20P + 0.20W + 0.15A + 0.15T + 0.10S + 0.10N + 0.10E), minus 10 for fatigue-list ideas without a rescue angle. Weights are re-mapped from rubric.json. Outputs a ranked table and IDEA.md.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Turns research into a defensible, rubric-aligned choice within 8% of the clock. It encodes the 2026 winner patterns (narrow domain pain, visible artifact, essential AI, narratable hard part).
recommendations.how: Write agents/idea-scorer.md and reuse the question bank from ECC skills/product-lens/SKILL.md Mode 1. Drop its long PRODUCT-BRIEF output in favour of a 1-page IDEA.md (template in §14.1 of the report).

recommendations.name: Checkpoint Workflow script
recommendations.what: Native Workflow script that enforces IDEA LOCK, SKELETON DEPLOYED, WOW WORKS, FEATURE FREEZE, VIDEO DONE and SUBMITTED at 8/30/55/75/85/92% of the event clock, with exit-criteria checks.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Organizers advise leaving 2-3 hours for video and submission, and teams reach about a quarter of their ambitions. Hard time-boxing is the main defense against scope creep and late submissions.
recommendations.how: hackforge.workflow.js reads the event start and deadline from rubric.json and gates each phase on artifacts: IDEA.md, a deployed URL returning 200, a green e2e run, the video URL plus a length check, and the submission checklist. It has variants for 24h, 48h and week-long events.

recommendations.why_for_hackforge: A broken live demo, an auth wall and live-API-only paths are the top failure modes. Anthropic's top weight is a demo that works and holds up live. The same Playwright script later drives the video recording.

It then validates the checklist: links live in incognito, video public and within the limit, licence present, no secrets, incremental commit history, word limits.

results.topic: Bright Data CLI (bdata 0.4.0) and Bright Data MCP (v3.1.0) cookbook for HackForge hackathon research
key_findings: Verified by running --help on every command and subcommand, plus 12 paid live calls. Measured spend: cli_unlocker zone went from $0.11 to $0.12, plus 13 pipeline records (about 13 credits).

`bdata search` without --country was localized to Mexico (gl=MX, en-MX). Always pass --country us --language en. Web results are in .organic[] (4.5 s, 22 KB); news results are in .news[], not .organic (13 s, 87 KB, mostly base64 images). Slim with jq before an agent reads either.

`bdata discover` returned HTTP 404 'Not found' in about 300 ms on both attempts, so Discover is not available to this account/key. `budget balance` also returns 403 for this scoped key. HackForge must treat discover as optional and fall back to search + scrape, and must keep its own credit ledger.

`bdata scrape` gave clean full Hacker News threads (13 KB markdown in 4.4 s). On www.reddit.com it returned only the post body with no comments, and old.reddit.com is blocked without KYC. Use the Reddit Posts pipeline for comments. `scrape --async` is a trap: 0.4.0 has no command to fetch the result.

`pipelines search`, `info` and `refresh` are free: they read a local catalog cache of 1,278 scrapers. Every record a pipeline returns is billed. Partial failures exit 0 (the GitHub run did), so every result needs a per-record .error check.

Pipeline latency varies a lot: Play Store reviews took 6 s for 5 records. A Reddit post took 163 s and returned 17 of 34 comments (top-level only, replies null, plus 26 related_posts). A YouTube video took 48 s via async and returned a 100 KB record with transcript, formatted_transcript and the top 20 comments. Reddit discover_by_keyword took 99 s and returned off-topic viral posts. GitHub discover_by_search_url took about 6.5 min and returned file-level records, one with an error.

Best research paths: Reddit pain points = SERP `site:reddit.com "<phrase>"`, then one async collect_by_url batch. Competitor gaps = Play/App Store/G2/Trustpilot review pipelines; the Play reviews test surfaced reviewers saying Mealime is shutting down. Idea-exists checks = free GitHub REST search + HN Algolia + SERP on producthunt.com and devpost.com/software.

The catalog has no Product Hunt, Hacker News, Devpost, Google Trends, Capterra or Stack Overflow scrapers. It does have Reddit, YouTube, X, TikTok, Instagram, LinkedIn, Threads, Bluesky, Crunchbase, G2, Trustpilot, app stores, Meta Ad Library, and ChatGPT/Perplexity/Google AI Mode answer scrapers.

Free alternatives beat Bright Data on two jobs: the HN Algolia API (under 1 s; per-year counts are a free trend proxy, e.g. 'vibe coding' had 0 HN stories in 2023-24 and 812 in Jan-Sep 2025) and the GitHub REST search API (under 1 s).

MCP v3.1.0 has 32 tools in groups: default/search (search_engine, scrape_as_markdown, discover), advanced_scraping (batch tools, scrape_as_html, extract, session_stats), scrapers (6 tools), browser (14), geo (2), and dataset search (2). The 'Rapid vs Pro' mode (&pro=1 / PRO_MODE) is legacy; all tools are on by default now and &groups= or &tools= limit them. The free tier is 5,000 credits/month shared with the CLI; PAYG is $1.50 per 1K for search/scrape and $8/GB for browser. A CONTENT_GATE option guards against prompt injection in scraped text.

`bdata add mcp` writes a local npx stdio entry with the API key in plaintext. --global writes ~/.claude.json, which works. --project writes ./.claude/settings.json, which is not where Claude Code reads project MCP servers (that is .mcp.json). The plugin's mcp-setup.md has the same mistake.

The client auto-retries 429/5xx 3 times with backoff up to 16 s. With --async, pipelines print {snapshot_id} on stdout and hints on stderr, and snapshots can be harvested later without re-billing. Running all pipelines async first and harvesting at the end is the right shape for a Workflow script.
ECC has no Bright Data integration (its deep-research skill uses Firecrawl and Exa MCPs), so structured Reddit, YouTube and app-store review mining is a HackForge differentiator.

recommendations.name: hf-web wrapper script
recommendations.what: A bash wrapper that is the only path agents use to call bdata. It forces --country us --language en on search, always writes with -o into .hackforge/web/<kind>_<slug>, returns cached files on a repeat request, logs each paid call to ledger.tsv, enforces HF_WEB_BUDGET (default 150 credits), runs verification gates (block-page grep, per-record .error count, non-empty results), and prints only slim JSON.
recommendations.why_for_hackforge: Prevents geo mislocalization, double-paying, context flooding from 22-100 KB JSON, and silent partial failures. The key can't read its balance (403), so local budget tracking is the only safeguard.

results.topic: HackForge packaging formats for Claude Code (CLI v2.1.x, docs as of 2026-10-15): skills, subagents, hooks, plugins and marketplaces, MCP config, and dynamic Workflow scripts, for shipping as an installable plugin and for manual copy into ~/.claude
key_findings: Plugin layout: .claude-plugin/plugin.json is the optional manifest and only name is required. Default component dirs sit at the plugin root: skills/<name>/SKILL.md, agents/*.md, commands/*.md (legacy), hooks/hooks.json, .mcp.json, workflows/*.js, bin/, settings.json. Manifest component paths must start with ./ and must resolve inside the plugin root.

Manifest override rules differ by key. skills adds to the default skills/ scan. commands, agents, outputStyles, workflows and experimental.themes REPLACE their default dirs. hooks and mcpServers MERGE with hooks/hooks.json and .mcp.json (a later server name replaces an earlier one). A CLAUDE.md at the plugin root is not loaded; put instructions in a skill.

Skills: a directory with SKILL.md plus supporting files. Locations are enterprise > personal (~/.claude/skills) > project (.claude/skills), plus nested and --add-dir dirs. Plugin skills are namespaced as /plugin-name:skill-name and cannot collide. Frontmatter includes name, description, when_to_use (description plus when_to_use is truncated at 1,536 chars in the listing), argument-hint, arguments, disable-model-invocation, user-invocable, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context: fork, agent, background, hooks, paths and shell. Args: $ARGUMENTS, $ARGUMENTS[N] or $N, and named $name. Also ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} for plugin skills.

Legacy .claude/commands/*.md still works and creates the same /name command as a skill. A skill wins over a command file of the same name. The docs recommend skills for new work because they add supporting files, invocation control and auto-loading.

Subagents: .claude/agents/*.md (project), ~/.claude/agents/*.md (user), plugin agents/*.md, plus --agents JSON for one session. Only name and description are required. Other fields include tools and disallowedTools, model (sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, a full ID, or inherit), permissionMode, maxTurns, skills (preload up to 32), mcpServers, hooks, memory (user, project or local), effort, isolation: worktree, and color. Plugin subagents IGNORE hooks, mcpServers and permissionMode, so ship hooks and MCP at plugin level.

Subagent tool restrictions: Workflow, Agent (at the depth limit), AskUserQuestion, EnterPlanMode and ScheduleWakeup are always removed from subagents. Default spawn nesting is 3 layers (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH). Concurrency defaults to 20 (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS).

Hooks: settings.json (user ~/.claude/settings.json, project .claude/settings.json, local .claude/settings.local.json, managed) and plugin hooks/hooks.json use event -> matcher group -> hooks array. Handler types are command, http, mcp_tool, prompt and agent (experimental). Matchers are exact or pipe-separated lists, or a JS regex otherwise (MCP tools are mcp__server__tool). About 33 events exist, including PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, SessionStart, Stop, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreCompact, Notification, FileChanged and SessionEnd.

Hook control: exit 0 means success (stdout JSON is parsed). Exit 2 is a blocking error and stderr is the reason. Any other non-zero exit is a non-blocking error (exit 1 does NOT block). Structured control uses hookSpecificOutput with hookEventName and, for PreToolUse, permissionDecision allow, deny, ask or defer plus updatedInput or additionalContext. Deny and ask permission rules still apply even when a hook returns allow. Plugin hooks use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, exec form (args) avoids quoting problems, and ${user_config.*} is rejected in shell-form hooks.

Plugin install from a local directory: claude plugin marketplace add ./dir (directory marketplace with .claude-plugin/marketplace.json), then claude plugin install name@marketplace with --scope user (default), project or local. Session-only testing uses claude --plugin-dir ./name, reloaded with /reload-plugins. claude plugin init name --with skills hooks mcp scaffolds into ~/.claude/skills/name as a name@skills-dir plugin. claude plugin validate <path> --strict exits 0 on pass, 1 on failure and 2 on unexpected error.

marketplace.json lives at <marketplace root>/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json and requires name, owner.name and plugins[]. Each plugin entry requires name and source. Relative sources such as ./plugins/hackforge resolve from the marketplace root and must start with ./. Other source types are github, url, git-subdir, npm, archive (with sha256) and command. Names starting with claude-, anthropic-, anthropics- or cc-plugin- are reserved and fail validation. hackforge is fine.

userConfig in plugin.json declares prompted values with types string, number, boolean, directory or file, each needing type, title and description. sensitive: true moves a value to the OS secure store. Values are referenced as ${user_config.KEY} in MCP config, exec-form hook args, and skill or agent body (sensitive values become placeholders there). Hooks also get CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> in their environment. Shell-form hook commands, monitor commands and headersHelper cannot use ${user_config.*}.

MCP: claude mcp add [--transport stdio|http|sse] [--scope local|project|user] [-e KEY=val] [--header 'H: v'] <name> -- <cmd> [args]. The default scope is local, which is stored in ~/.claude.json under the project path. Project scope writes .mcp.json at the project root. User scope is also stored in ~/.claude.json, not in ~/.claude/settings.json. .mcp.json supports ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} in command, args, env, url and headers. An entry with url but no type is skipped as a config error (it is read as stdio).

MCP context control: tool search is on by default and defers MCP tool definitions. ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH takes unset, true, auto, auto:N (N percent of context) or false. A server or tool can set alwaysLoad: true to load upfront. MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS defaults to 25,000 tokens (warning at 10,000). Text results over 50,000 characters are saved to a file regardless of that setting.

MCP permission rules have no parentheses: mcp__<server> and mcp__<server>__* match all tools of a server, and mcp__<server>__<tool> matches one tool. A rule with parentheses in an mcp__ entry is skipped with a warning. Plugin server tools are named mcp__plugin_<plugin>_<server>__<tool>. Evaluation order is deny, then ask, then allow, and the first match wins.

Workflows are documented as dynamic workflows (docs/en/workflows.md). Scripts start with export const meta = { name, description } as a pure literal, and the body uses agent(prompt, opts), parallel(), pipeline(items, fn), phase(title), log(msg) and the global args. Saved locations are .claude/workflows/ (project), ~/.claude/workflows/ (personal) and <plugin>/workflows/ (plugin, run as /plugin:name). Invoke with the /name slash command, /workflows for runs, or the Workflow tool with script, name, scriptPath (wins over the others), args and resumeFromRunId. Date.now(), Math.random() and no-arg new Date() throw. Limits: 16 concurrent agents by default (raise with CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS up to 256), 1,000 agents per run, and 4,096 items per parallel or pipeline call. Requires paid plan, API, Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry, and can be disabled with disableWorkflows or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_WORKFLOWS=1.

Undocumented or unverified in the pages read: the exact saved-filename rule (docs show .js, and the command name comes from meta.name, not the filename); the Workflow tool's return/output shape; the parallel() signature; the agent() model option key; precedence when a saved or plugin workflow shares a name with a bundled one such as /deep-research (this environment also has a user skill named deep-research); and the minimum Claude Code version for plugin-shipped workflows (the docs give 2.1.248 for /workflow-authoring and 2.1.269 for the concurrency env var only).
